PGCtest (CompTestER) normal-product test on a phenotype pair

Source: vignettes/method-pgctest.Rmd
method-pgctest.Rmd

Function: run_pgctest()

Result column: pgctest

Family: Pairwise product-Z composite test

Introduction

Pairwise (traits i,ji,j) pleiotropy screen based on the normal-product statistic |Z1Z2||Z_1 Z_2|, with a Bessel-K0K_0 tail CDF and an empirical variance normalization. In this package, the implemented routine applies a product-Z tail calibration with one empirical scale; it is evaluated for one trait pair at a time.

Mathematical Framework and Implementation

For variant vv let Z1,Z2Z_1, Z_2 be the per-trait Z-scores (β̂/sê\hat\beta/\widehat{\mathrm{se}}) and let X=|Z1Z2|X = |Z_1 Z_2|. The implemented test rejects for large product magnitude XX after calibration against the normal-product reference distribution; it does not explicitly evaluate a multi-component composite-null mixture.

Standard normal-product tail. When Z1,Z2Z_1, Z_2 are independent standard normal, the density of X=|Z1Z2|X = |Z_1 Z_2| is

f(x)=2πK0(x),x≥0, f(x) = \frac{2}{\pi}\, K_0(x), \qquad x \ge 0,

with K0K_0 the modified Bessel function of the second kind of order 0. The implementation builds the corresponding survival (upper-tail) function once,

S(x)=Pr⁡(X≥x)=∫x∞2πK0(u)du, S(x) = \Pr(X \ge x) = \int_x^{\infty} \frac{2}{\pi} K_0(u)\, du,

by evaluating ff on a degree-10 power-spaced grid (xi=xmax(i/(len−1))10x_i = x_{\max}\,(i/(\mathrm{len}-1))^{10}, dense near 0) and accumulating a reverse-cumulative trapezoidal integral, normalized so that S(0)=1S(0)=1; the grid upper bound is xmax=2max⁡vXvx_{\max}=2\max_v X_v.

Empirical variance normalization. Because the per-trait Z-scores need not be exactly standard normal (inflation, residual cross-trait dependence), the observed statistic is rescaled before being passed to S(⋅)S(\cdot). With sample variances Var̂(Z1)\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(Z_1) and Var̂(Z2)\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(Z_2) over all variants, define

d=Var̂(Z1)+Var̂(Z2)−1, d = \sqrt{\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(Z_1) + \widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(Z_2) - 1},

and report the p-value by linear interpolation of the tail CDF at the rescaled point

p=S(|Z1Z2|d). p = S\!\left(\frac{|Z_1 Z_2|}{d}\right).

A signed pleiotropy z is also computed internally as z=sign(Z1Z2)Φ−1(1−p/2)z = \mathrm{sign}(Z_1 Z_2)\,\Phi^{-1}(1 - p/2); the R wrapper returns the p-value component ($pp).

What This Method Advances

PGCtest uses the product of two trait Z-scores and calibrates that product under a normal-product reference distribution.

Assumptions

  • Under the relevant null the per-trait Z-scores are approximately standard normal, so that |Z1Z2||Z_1 Z_2| follows the 2πK0\tfrac{2}{\pi}K_0 normal-product law.
  • Mild departures (variance inflation, weak dependence) are corrected by the single empirical scale dd; the correction assumes the inflation is well summarized by the marginal Z variances.
  • Independence of Z1,Z2Z_1, Z_2 is assumed by the base tail; strong cross-trait correlation is not separately modelled (unlike PLACO, which carries an explicit rr).
  • Variants are treated as exchangeable for the variance estimates.

When This Method Is a Good Fit

Good for pairwise product-Z evidence when product-tail calibration is appropriate.

The implemented PGCtest wrapper returns only the pp values from the C++ routine. The C++ routine also computes signed zz scores internally, but they are not attached to pleio@results. The product-tail calibration uses only the two Z-score vectors and their marginal sample variances; it does not explicitly model cross-trait correlation and relies on a positive variance denominator.

Pairwise methods use i and j to select the two phenotypes. Re-run the method for each phenotype pair that should be tested.

Minimal Usage 

library(pleioverse)
set.seed(1)
pleio <- run_pleiosim(
  n_phenotype = 3, n_participant = 500,
  n_variant_pleiotropic = 3,
  n_variant_nonpleiotropic = c(3, 3, 3),
  n_variant_null = 30,
  heritability = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3)
)
pleio <- run_pgctest(pleio, i = 1, j = 2)
head(pleio@results$pgctest)

Implementation Files

  • R wrapper: R/run_pgctest.R
  • C++ kernel or dispatcher: src/pgctest.cpp
  • Shared MPAT inputs, where applicable: R/pleiotest.R and src/test_engine.cpp
